{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2024}} {{Infobox award | name = 2013 FIFA Ballon d'Or | subheader = | image = Cristiano Ronaldo, 2012 2.JPG | image_size = | alt = | caption = 2013 FIFA Ballon d'Or winner, Cristiano Ronaldo | awarded_for = | date = {{start date|2014|01|13|df=y}} | location = [[Zürich]], Switzerland | country = Switzerland | presenter = [[FIFA]] | host = | former name = | preshow_host = | acts = | website = {{URL|ballondor.com}} | runtime = | award1_type = Won by | award1_winner= {{flagicon|POR}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] (2nd [[Ballon d'Or]]) | previous = [[2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2012]] | main = [[FIFA Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[2014 FIFA Ballon d'Or|2014]] }} The '''2013 [[FIFA Ballon d'Or]]''' ({{lit|'''2013 FIFA Golden Ball'''}}), was the fourth year for [[FIFA]]'s awards for the top football players and coaches of the year. The awards were given out in [[Zürich]] on 13 January 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/playeroftheyear/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111022033859/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/playeroftheyear/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 October 2011|title=Ballon d'Or 2013|date=29 October 2013 |work=FIFA|access-date=29 October 2013 }} The deadline for voting was 15 November 2013 but was extended to 29 November 2013 for the first time in history. Portuguese winger [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] won the [[FIFA Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]] award as the World Player of the Year. It was his second Ballon d'Or, after winning the award in [[2008 Ballon d'Or|2008]], as well as his first FIFA Ballon d'Or. [[Nadine Angerer]] was announced as the Women's World Player of the Year recipient, while [[Jupp Heynckes]] claimed the World Coach of the Year for Men's Football, and [[Silvia Neid]] the World Coach of the Year for Women's Football. The ninety-minute ceremony was hosted by [[Fernanda Lima]] along with [[Ruud Gullit]].{{cite news |first=Brian |last=Homewood |title=Emotional Ronaldo ends Messi run
